title: Addressing Issues That Limit Artistic Expression in Everyday Places
what_it_is: Addressing Issues That Limit Artistic Expression in Everyday Places

sections.label: Enriching debate experience
sections.summary: The speaker says the debates were a very enriching experience.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Through all these debates, we have actually felt that it was a very, very enriching experience.

sections.label: Purpose-built art spaces
sections.summary: Purpose-built art spaces such as the Esplanade, National Gallery Singapore, Singapore Arts Museum, The Substation and Centre 42 are crucial.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
sentences.text: Purpose-built art spaces are crucial, like the Esplanade, National Gallery Singapore, Singapore Arts Museum, The Substation, Centre 42, amongst others.

sections.label: The Garden and permissions
sections.summary: The Garden needed no permissions, and its users gave one another permission to try things, be different, disagree, agree and gather.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
sentences.text: The Garden was a place that needed no permissions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
sentences.text: In fact, many years later, I realised that the people who used the Garden, whether the artist or the audience, gave permission to one another to try things, to be different, to disagree, to agree and, most importantly, to gather.

sections.label: Laws conditioning mindsets
sections.summary: Laws like the Public Order Act and permit requirements have conditioned mindsets and made people fearful, though forum theatre in public spaces has occurred without incidents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
sentences.text: The many laws, like Public Order Act, that caution people from gathering, from getting together for a cause, permits and permissions needed to express, to perform, all these narratives that Singapore needs to be orderly have conditioned our mindset, inhibiting us, making us fearful of being spontaneous: what if I break the law, what if people get offended, what if people complain?

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
sentences.text: Forum theatre in the heartlands dealing with difficult issues, like end-of-life concerns, discriminations of migrant workers, domestic violence, all these have happened in public spaces without incidents.

sections.label: Blindfolded train licence question
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether a group would be permitted to blindfold themselves and sit silently in the train holding a book.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
sentences.text: If a group had applied for a licence to blindfold themselves and sit in the train silently, holding the book "This Is What Inequality Looks Like", would that be permitted?

sections.label: Independent body for art disputes
sections.summary: The speaker proposes an independent body with legal experts, artistic personnel and stakeholders to address art disputes, investigate complaints and set up dialogues.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
sentences.text: Our people need more space and support to initiate artistic and cultural activities from the ground-up, with the Government playing a more catalytic role in facilitating connections and allowing emergent subcultures and creative communities to thrive.” I support the Government in this vision.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
sentences.text: But we know that while we are at the infancy of this development, there have been disputes and disagreement like the "Golden Staircase", Mr Oh’s installation at the void deck in Chong Pang, amongst others.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
sentences.text: So, here I would humbly like to propose that the Government should form an independent body, almost like an ombudsman, to look at such disagreements.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
sentences.text: The independent body should include legal experts, artistic personnel and various stakeholders to address these disagreements, to investigate complaints, but, importantly, to set up dialogues and conversations between complainants and the artists.

sections.label: Public art efforts in Singapore
sections.summary: PAssionArts takes place in every constituency, and the Government has run various efforts to increase public art over 30 years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: I am sure PAssionArts is quite familiar to many of the Members sitting around the House, because it is taking place in every constituency in Singapore – in everyday spaces, in hawker centres, void decks, community centres and parks.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: These offerings are part of the over 100 arts and cultural events available each day, and which 74% of Singaporeans agreed they were proud of in the 2015 Population Survey on the Arts.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: The Government has embarked on a variety of efforts to increase public art over the last 30 years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: These include the Urban Redevelopment Authority’s Public Sculpture Masterplan and Art Incentive Scheme, the Land Transport Authority’s Art in Transit Programme, NHB’s Public Art Tax Incentive Scheme, and the NAC’s establishment of the Public Art Trust (PAT) in 2014 with a $10 million seed fund from the Ministry of Culture, Community and Youth (MCCY).

sections.label: PAssionArts 2017 participation figures
sections.summary: In 2017, PAssionArts involved about 50,000 arts participants and volunteers in more than 65 heartland locations.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: In 2017, PAssionArts involved some 50,000 arts participants and volunteers, about 30 arts groups and 300 organisations, including schools, voluntary welfare organisations, religious groups, community groups, and hospitals in more than 65 heartland locations.

sections.label: New Bicentennial public artworks commissioned
sections.summary: Two new public artworks will be commissioned in community spaces for Singapore's Bicentennial, and NAC plans one more each year thereafter.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: Another two new public artworks will be commissioned in community spaces to commemorate Singapore's Bicentennial next year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: And NAC plans to commission one additional public artwork each year thereafter.

sections.label: Ang Mo Kio public art activities
sections.summary: Site-specific works by four Singaporean artists reached over 190,000 people and showed how public art can bring communities together.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: The site-specific works by four Singaporean artists included talks, live painting sessions and hands-on craft activities for residents and non-residents of Ang Mo Kio to learn about the rich history and hidden characteristics of this neighbourhood.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: These activities reached over 190,000 people and demonstrated how public art can engage and bring communities together when it is carefully curated.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: As a result of the combined efforts of the Government, private, public and people sectors, today, a wide range and diversity of visual and performing arts have enlivened our public spaces.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: The Government will continue to develop our policies so that Singapore is home to diverse and distinctive arts that are accessible to, and inspire our people and connect our communities.
